title: The older Reformed answer more simply
source_text: LXII. Sed vetustiores Scholae Reformatae Doctores simplicius respondent gratiam non tollere a voluntate libertatem, licet aliquam ei necessitatem imponat, quia non omnis necessitas cum libertate pugnat, sed ea solum quae est a vi externa, vel a naturali determinatione. Gratia vero voluntatem non cogit, neque vim ei ullam affert, sed illam suaviter flectit, & modo qui est ejus naturae consentaneus.
pass_a_gloss: LXII. But the older Doctors of the Reformed School answer more simply that grace does not take away freedom from the will, although it imposes some necessity on it, because not every necessity conflicts with freedom, but only that which is from external force, or from natural determination. But grace does not compel the will, nor brings any force on it, but bends it sweetly, & in a manner which is agreeable to its nature.
pass_b_english: Thesis LXII. The older teachers of the Reformed school give a simpler answer. Grace does not take freedom away from the will, even though it lays a certain necessity on it, because not every necessity is at odds with freedom, only the necessity that comes from outside force or from natural determination.
Grace does not compel the will or do it any violence; it bends it gently, in a way that suits its nature.
